subject: The gun-side AI bots: the class family behind the five ticks that turn a unit's fire target into gun angles and a trigger, how one is attached to a gun and given a skill, and what the gun's aim step consumes afterwards.
reuses: include/bsp/bot_fire_target.hpp for the 008FEF40 debounce, the 008FDAF0 angle pair and the 008FFA20 hysteresis constants
include/bsp/gun_aiming.hpp for kGunAimOffTargetHorzAngle, kGunAimOffHorzAngle and the 0085ABA0 / 0085AD80 contract
docs/FIXED_STEP_JOB_WAVES.md for 008759B0, the sub-list walker that calls slot +0Ch with 0.05f
docs/GUN_CLASS_FAMILY.md for the weapon descriptor sub-type at [gun+3F4h]+80h and the class ids 20h-27h

open_questions: The property-name blocks of the AAGunnerBot, AAFlakBot and TorpedoBot classes at 00D180F0-00D18218 and 00D18288 were not attributed to offsets; their visitors are 008FE800/008FE8F0, 008FF060/008FF130 and 008FF360/008FF400.

Where the skill-record arrays begin inside the class descriptors. The class names are settled but the objects are not: 00900AF0 and the ledger's read_<name>_parameters_* routines (008FC6D0, 008FCA10, 008FCD60, 008FCF30, 008FD370, 008FD640, 008FD880, 009973B0) are contract: unread. Only descriptor-relative offsets are proven.
The meaning of the four skill scalars passed to the target entity's vtable[100h], and of the (0.6,0.6,0.6) direction at 00CE3D30 every caller passes as the second argument.
gun+474h and 008FDBE0, the pair 009030C0 uses at 0090330d and 0090331b.
Whether bit 1 of [unit+634h] means 'a human is aiming this gun'. 009030C0 tests bit 0, 006DF520 tests bit 1, 2 or 3 by muzzle kind, and 008FFF20 tests bit 2.
006FDF60, the vtable[1F0h] immediate fire that 008FFF20 and 006DF520 use; it exists only on the turning-gun vtables, the base 00CFE0A8 ending at +1ECh.

Who reads the weapon director's allowFire byte at director+3Ch. Proven here to be none of 008FFF20, 00959C20 or 00864FE0; a byte-pattern scan for the three plausible encodings of a byte load at displacement 3Ch found no reader. Handed back to the weapon director's owner.
008FC080, DepthChargeBot's tick, and the ArtillerySubDirectorBot and PilotBot classes at [00E19994] and [00F8A30C].

tool_problems.symptom: the row {address: 006df623, native: 006deff0} reports 'callee 006deff0 is not a Ghidra function' although Ghidra does have a function there, body 006deff0-006df12b. 184 of 185 rows pass; this is the only failure.
tool_problems.cause: line 90 accepts the live get_function_by_address response only when "'error' not in text.lower()". The response carries the function's NAME, and once the integrator applied this packet's ledger name BSP_GunBot_RerollAimErrorEnvelope to Ghidra, the substring 'Error' in the name made the guard treat a good response as a bridge error. The same row passed before the name was applied.
tool_problems.fix: tighten the guard so it matches an actual error response rather than any occurrence of the word, for example a leading 'error:' or the bridge's own error key, instead of a bare substring test over the whole payload. Any future symbol containing 'error' hits this.
tool_problems.workaround: none applied. The name is accurate: the class's own property strings at 006DF260 are 'Error' and 'ErrorOffset', so the routine that rolls that envelope is named for them. Renaming to dodge the substring would hide the defect.
